prompt:
solution.py is meant to implement the specification below, but it contains several defects. One has been reported: `from_roman("IIII")` returns 4 instead of raising ValueError. Fix that and every other deviation from the specification. Keep the public names and signatures unchanged and do not change behaviour the specification requires.

Specification: Implement `to_roman(number)` and `from_roman(text)` in solution.py. `to_roman` converts an int from 1 to 3999 into its standard upper-case Roman numeral (subtractive forms IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM). It raises ValueError outside that range and TypeError when the argument is not an int (bool is rejected too). `from_roman` accepts exactly the strings `to_roman` can produce and returns the int; every other string raises ValueError, including the empty string, lower case, surrounding spaces and non-standard forms such as IIII, VV, IL, IC, XM, IXI or MMMM.
acceptance: bool is not an int here
